$comment: The token migrations, as data. See migrations.d.mts for the schema and migrations.test.mjs for the check that keeps this file honest. Authored by hand; verified against token-baseline.json.

migrations.reason: --status-warning is 1.87:1 on --bg in light. Yellow that clears 3:1 on white is olive, which is not a caution colour, so the SC 1.4.11 floor is carried by a separate token instead of by the fill. The fill is still --status-warning; the edge around it is --status-warning-border (3.76:1 light, 11.22:1 dark).
migrations.guidance: Keep the fill. Move only the edge.

migrations.reason: --fg-on-signal was named for a ramp step (--signal-*) that the palette dial now owns, and it resolved to --ink-1000 — ink, which is only the right foreground under a palette whose accent is light. It survives as a documented alias of --accent-fg and collapses under any non-default palette. --accent-fg is the same colour under the default palette and the correct one under every other.
migrations.guidance: A straight rename. The rendered colour does not move under the default `ember` palette.

migrations.reason: Neither --fg-inverse nor --fg-on-signal can be correct on a status fill in both themes, because both move with the theme while the fill under them does not. --fg-inverse is white in light and black in dark; on the previous token set it already failed two cells, and against the re-picked hues it would fail three. Each state now ships the foreground measured against its own fill: --status-success-on, --status-warning-on, --status-danger-on, --status-info-on, holding 5.17 / 11.22 / 5.41 / 5.06 across every palette x theme combination.
migrations.guidance: Replace with the -on token of whichever status fill this text sits on. This is never rewritten for you: the tool can see that a status token is mentioned nearby, but not which fill this element is actually painted with, and guessing the wrong state would trade a contrast bug for a colour bug.

migrations.reason: Status used to be made of brand. --status-success was var(--anchor-500) — forest — and --status-warning was var(--signal-600), the identical amber as the primary CTA, so a caution badge sat next to an accent button in the same colour. Both now own a palette-independent hue and neither moves with the brand.
migrations.guidance: The token name did not change, so nothing here is rewritten. Look at each of these and decide which one you meant: if you wanted the brand colour (a badge deliberately matched to a button) use --anchor or --accent explicitly; if you wanted the status, keep the status token and accept the new hue.

migrations.reason: The rest of each status set was re-picked alongside the two fills above so that every member of a set is measured against the same hue. The shifts are small — danger moved 25deg to 27deg, info 240deg to 250deg — and every pair still clears its threshold, so there is nothing to change.
migrations.guidance: No action. Reported as a count so that a visual diff against these colours has an explanation.

migrations.reason: The neutral ramp is mixed from two palette-owned dials now — oklch(<L>% calc(<C> * var(--n-mult)) var(--n-h)) — rather than from literal hue and chroma. Lightness is untouched, and lightness is what carries contrast: across every neutral foreground on every neutral surface in both themes the largest disagreement between the two shipped palettes is 0.003:1. The declared values moved; the rendered colours did not.
migrations.guidance: No action, and nothing is reported. The entry exists so that this claim is on the record and so a later, genuinely visible repoint of one of these tokens cannot hide among them.
